name: four devices preserve rank order and route work through the communicator
test:
import numpy as np
BaseCommunicator = Communicator
class RecordingCommunicator(BaseCommunicator):
    sends = []
    receives = []
    def send(self, src, dst, data):
        type(self).sends.append((src, dst, np.asarray(data).shape))
        super().send(src, dst, data)
    def recv(self, dst):
        type(self).receives.append(dst)
        return super().recv(dst)
Communicator = RecordingCommunicator
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
a = rng.normal(size=(12, 6))
b = rng.normal(size=(6, 8))
assert np.allclose(dp_mat_mul(a, b, 4), a @ b)
assert RecordingCommunicator.sends
assert RecordingCommunicator.receives
RecordingCommunicator.sends.clear()
RecordingCommunicator.receives.clear()
assert np.allclose(fsdp_mat_mul(a, b, 4), a @ b)
assert len(RecordingCommunicator.sends) >= 20
assert len(RecordingCommunicator.receives) >= 20

name: one device works and invalid partitions are rejected
input: one-device matrix product and malformed shapes
test:
import numpy as np
a = np.arange(12.0).reshape(6, 2)
b = np.arange(8.0).reshape(2, 4)
assert np.allclose(dp_mat_mul(a, b, 1), a @ b)
assert np.allclose(fsdp_mat_mul(a, b, 1), a @ b)
for call in [
    lambda: dp_mat_mul(np.ones(2), np.ones((2, 2)), 1),
    lambda: fsdp_mat_mul(np.ones((3, 2)), np.ones((3, 2)), 1),
    lambda: dp_mat_mul(np.ones((3, 2)), np.ones((2, 4)), 2),
    lambda: fsdp_mat_mul(np.ones((4, 2)), np.ones((2, 5)), 2),
    lambda: dp_mat_mul(np.ones((2, 2)), np.ones((2, 2)), 0),
]:
    try:
        call()
        assert False, 'expected ValueError'
    except ValueError:
        pass
